question.text: Consider a hydrogen atom with its electron in the <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi></mrow></msup></math> orbital. An electromagnetic radiation of wavelength 90 nm is used to ionize the atom. If the kinetic energy of the ejected electron is 10.4 eV, then the value of n is <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1242</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>

solution.text:
EPh=hcλ=124290=13.8 eV
EPh=∆E+(K.E.)
13.8=∆E+10.4
∆E=3.4 eV
So electron initially was in n=2
